title: A refused value in the hidden Festanstellung block makes Speichern fail without a word
evidence: With "Festanstellung ausschließen" on, ProfileEditor.svelte:676-737 (`{#if !c.noPermanent}`) removes minSalary, permanentRemoteMin and permanentPlaces from the DOM, but their values stay in `editor.after` and go into every save. When the backend refuses one of them, ProfileView.svelte:214-220 sets only `fieldError` (never `saveNote`), and `focusField` (ProfileEditor.svelte:222-230) finds no `[data-field="minSalary"]`, so it focuses nothing. The Field that would render the error is not mounted, so the save bar (ProfileEditor.svelte:790-811) keeps showing "Nicht gespeichert" and gives no reason. The leave dialog's "Speichern" fails the same way (saveAndLeave returns silently). Backend probe (scratch crate calling jobalert_core::profile): a file with {"ausgeschlossene_vertragsarten":["Festanstellung"],"min_jahresgehalt":20000000} reads as no_permanent=true, min_salary=Some(20000000). Changing only the name and saving gives `save refused: Invalid(ProfileValue { field: "minSalary", row: None })`. So no edit of that profile can ever be saved (form.rs validate MAX_SALARY 10_000_000; the reader does not clamp it). The same path is reachable from the UI alone: NumberField does not clamp, and the block's unreadable-value notes also hide while the head still says "Etwas prüfen".
repro: Profil: type 150 into "Mindest-Remote-Anteil", turn "Festanstellung ausschließen" on, press Speichern. With the real backend the save is refused for permanentRemoteMin, and the page shows only "Nicht gespeichert" with no field, no note and no focus. Closing the window then only offers Speichern (fails again) or Verwerfen (loses every edit).
fix: When the refused field is not rendered, say the error in the save bar (set saveNote to errorText(error)), or show the Festanstellung block while it holds a fieldError or a FieldProblem. Also consider validating or clamping the hidden numbers client-side, like the reader clamps the percent.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium. I patched the stub's save_profile in the served bundle to refuse permanentRemoteMin > 100, the same way core's validate does (form.rs:496-518 checks min_salary and permanent_remote_min whether or not no_permanent is set, and normalized() keeps both values). Steps: default scenario, typed 150 into Mindest-Remote-Anteil, turned Festanstellung ausschließen on, pressed Speichern. The request carried permanentRemoteMin=150 with noPermanent=true. Afterwards the bar said only "Nicht gespeichert", there was no profile-save-error, no field had aria-invalid=true, and the focus stayed on Speichern (focusField finds no [data-field=permanentRemoteMin]). The leave dialog's Speichern made a second refused call, the dialog closed silently and the status stayed "Nicht gespeichert". Side effect: in the default scenario the Festanstellung block holds an unreadable value ("viel"), so the same toggle also hides that note while the badge still lists it.
verifierNotes.betterFix: 1) Let ProfileEditor.focusField return whether it found and focused the field. In ProfileView.save(), when the refused field is not rendered, set saveNote = () => errorText(error), so the bar names the field ("Der Wert bei „Mindest-Remote-Anteil“ passt nicht.") and saveAndLeave's failure is explained too. 2) Stop the hidden values from blocking a save in the first place. Either skip the range check (and the write) for min_salary, permanent_remote_min and permanent_places in validate while no_permanent is on, or cap NumberField input at the backend maxima for salary and percent so no out-of-range value can be typed. Showing the Festanstellung block while the switch says it is excluded would contradict the switch, so avoid that option.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium and WebKit. I patched the stub so it refuses permanentRemoteMin > 100 the way core's validate does (form.rs MAX_PERCENT; save_form validates the whole `after`, hidden fields included); script t01.js. With 150 in Mindest-Remote-Anteil, the visible case shows the error at the field and focuses it. After turning "Festanstellung ausschließen" on and saving, save_profile still sends permanentRemoteMin 150 and the refusal comes back. The status line then reads only "Nicht gespeichert": no alert, no focus (Chromium keeps it on Speichern, WebKit falls back to BODY). Speichern in the leave dialog closes the dialog and fails silently in the same way. The code agrees: ProfileView.save sets only fieldError, and the Field is not mounted inside `{#if !c.noPermanent}`. The reader does not clamp min_salary, so a file whose min_jahresgehalt is above 10,000,000 with Festanstellung excluded can never be saved. Screenshot: verify-ui-forms-2/t01-chromium-hidden-refused.png.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Have focusField return whether it found `[data-field=...]`. When it did not, set saveNote to errorText(error), so the save bar says why. Better still, show the Festanstellung block while fieldError or a FieldProblem targets minSalary, permanentRemoteMin or permanentPlaces. Also cap the percent NumberField at 100 on the client, the same limit the reader applies.

title: Ctrl/Cmd+S saves the profile without the text typed into a chip field
evidence: input.ts:576-579 runs the form's `shortcut` (ProfileEditor save()) directly. ChipInput only commits its draft on Enter or on blur (ChipInput.svelte:158-171), so the draft is never in `editor.after` when the shortcut fires. Live, Chromium and WebKit, default scenario: (A) type "Kanban" into Werkzeuge und Methoden: Speichern stays disabled with "Noch nichts geändert.", and Ctrl+S saves nothing (0 save_profile calls). (C) change the name, type "Miro" into Werkzeuge, press Ctrl+S: save_profile.after.tools = ["SAP S/4HANA","LucaNet","Power BI"] (no Miro), the bar says "Gespeichert, Jobs neu bewertet." while "Miro" still sits in the field; leaving the field turns it into a chip and the bar flips to "Nicht gespeichert". A mouse click on Speichern works because its pointerdown blurs the field first. Side note: PLAN Decisions "Keys" says the app's own shortcuts are exactly two (Ctrl/Cmd+F, Ctrl/Cmd+Z); this Ctrl/Cmd+S is not listed there.
repro: ?platform=windows, Profil, change Name, click into Werkzeuge und Methoden, type Miro, press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS).
fix: Before the shortcut saves, commit the focused chip field (for example blur the active element, or have ChipInput register a commit hook the form calls). Count a non-empty chip draft as a change for Speichern's disabled state. Document Ctrl/Cmd+S under Keys, or drop it.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium and WebKit. (A) With only "Kanban" typed into Werkzeuge und Methoden, Speichern stays aria-disabled and Ctrl+S makes 0 save_profile calls. (C) After changing the name and typing "Miro", Ctrl+S saved tools ["SAP S/4HANA","LucaNet","Power BI"] without Miro and the bar said "Gespeichert, Jobs neu bewertet." with "Miro" still in the field. On blur the bar flipped to "Nicht gespeichert". The code agrees: input.ts:575-579 runs the form shortcut without committing the chip draft, and ChipInput commits only on Enter or blur. The side note also holds: PLAN Decisions "Keys" says the app's own shortcuts are exactly two (Ctrl/Cmd+F and Ctrl/Cmd+Z). Ctrl/Cmd+S appears in input.ts:203 and in the ProfileEditor doc comment but nowhere in PLAN.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Keep the fix inside input.ts: on isSaveShortcut, first run the commit handler of a focused chip field (the chipKeys handlers input.ts already holds), then the form's shortcut after a tick, so the caret stays where it is. Blurring the field would also work but moves the focus. Then make the PLAN/code conflict a user decision: either add "Ctrl/Cmd+S saves the profile form" to the Keys row, or drop the shortcut, since the binding row says exactly two. Making a pending draft count as a change is optional.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium and WebKit (t02.js). (A) With only "Kanban" typed into Werkzeuge, Speichern stays disabled and Ctrl+S makes 0 save_profile calls. (C) After changing the name and typing Miro, Ctrl+S saves tools without Miro and the bar says "Gespeichert, Jobs neu bewertet." while Miro is still in the field. Blurring the field then turns the bar back to "Nicht gespeichert". A mouse press works, even on the disabled Speichern, because pointerdown blurs the field and commits the draft first (t02b.js). The side note also holds: Ctrl/Cmd+S (input.ts isSaveShortcut) is not in PLAN Decisions "Keys", which says the app's own shortcuts are exactly two.
verifierNotes.betterFix: In input.ts, before handlerFor(target,'shortcut') runs, call the focused chip field's own commit (the chipKeys handler for event.target, with the same single-match rule as blur for option fields). That keeps the caret in place, whereas blurring would drop it. Then either add Ctrl/Cmd+S to PLAN "Keys" as a form key or remove it.

title: Country names the Profil view offers make a file's whole country list unreadable, and the first edit drops the rest
evidence: Since 8ee3696 a profile may name countries in words, but country_code (facts.rs) only knows lex::COUNTRIES (engine.rs:1356-1397). That table has no name for DK, FI, HR, NO, SI or SK, and misses English names the UI shows (Belgium, Luxembourg, Czechia, Denmark, Norway, Finland...). The UI offers all 25 by name in both languages (de.ts profile.country, en.ts countryName), and core/tests/countries.rs checks only the codes. Probe with the real core: laender ["Deutschland","Norwegen"] gives countries=[] plus CriterionNotUnderstood with value "[\"Deutschland\",\"Norwegen\"]". ["Dänemark"], ["Belgium"], ["Luxembourg"], ["Czechia"] and ["Finnland"] give the same, while ["Großbritannien"] reads GB. So the country exclusion is off for such a file, and the note shows the raw JSON array. As soon as the user adds any country, fieldProblems (profile.svelte.ts:280-284) treats the value as replaced and the note goes. The save then writes only the new list, and Deutschland and Norwegen are gone without a word (live, profile-unreadable: after adding Deutschland, countries-unread = 0 and save.after.criteria.countries = ["DE"], clear = []).
repro: Put "harte_kriterien": {"laender": ["Deutschland", "Norwegen"]} in beraterprofil.json and open Profil: Einsatzländer is empty with „["Deutschland","Norwegen"]“ ... nicht lesen. Click "DACH hinzufügen" and save: Norwegen is gone from the file.
fix: Derive the engine's name table from one list covering every code of country_codes with its German and English name (plus the aliases UK, England, USA...). Add a core test that every name in both catalogs reads back to its code. Better still, keep the known entries and report only the unknown ones instead of dropping the whole list.

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. country_code (facts.rs:119-131) looks for an exact folded name in lex::COUNTRIES (engine.rs:1356-1397). That table has no entry for DK, FI, HR, NO, SI or SK, nor for the English catalog names Belgium, Luxembourg, Czechia (only "czech"), Denmark, Norway, Finland, Croatia, Slovenia and Slovakia, or the German Dänemark, Norwegen, Finnland, Kroatien, Slowenien and Slowakei. countries_of collects with Option, so one unknown name makes the whole list None, which is reported as criterionNotUnderstood. core/tests/countries.rs compares only the codes. Real-world impact is limited because the UI and the CV prompt (prompt.rs:106) write codes, so only hand-written files or files from before 8ee3696 are affected. "The first edit drops the rest" is the documented general behaviour for any unreadable value (fieldProblems treats a changed value as replaced). It becomes a problem here only because the names are valid countries the engine should know.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Build the engine's name table from one list keyed by every code of profile::country_codes(), with its German and English catalog names plus the aliases (UK, England, USA, Vereinigte Staaten...). Extend core/tests/countries.rs, which already parses both catalogs, so that every catalog name reads back to its code through country_code. Keep the all-or-nothing reading: keeping the known entries of a partly unknown list would narrow the allowed countries and wrongly exclude jobs (for example in Norway), which 8ee3696 deliberately avoided.

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. facts.rs country_code maps names only through lex::COUNTRIES. That table has no entry for DK, FI, HR, NO, SI or SK, and no Belgium, Luxembourg or Czechia (only "czech"), yet country_codes() offers all of them from CITIES and both catalogs name them. collect::<Option<Vec>> turns one unknown name into None for the whole list. The value then goes to not_understood and the form's countries become []. fieldProblems drops the note once the countries field changes, and merge writes only the new list, so a meaningful file list such as ["Deutschland","Norwegen"] disappears on the first edit. This goes against PLAN's "a country of a file the app does not know stays". I did not rerun the Rust probe; the code path is unambiguous.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Add the missing German and English names and aliases to COUNTRIES. This is an engine change: bump ENGINE_VERSION and update the golden digest, because the table also scans job locations. Add a core test that reads every name in de.ts profile.country and en.ts countryName and checks that country_code gives its code back. Do not keep the known entries and silently drop the unknown ones: that would narrow the allowed countries and create wrong exclusions. Instead, have form::read keep each entry (a known name as its code, an unknown one as written, which ChipInput shows as a raw chip) while the engine keeps treating a list with an unknown entry as not understood.

title: "Weiter zum ersten Abruf" is offered for a profile the setup does not count
evidence: ProfileView.svelte:69 `const next = $derived(saved && app.state?.firstRun ? () => navigation.go('jobs') : null)` ignores whether the saved profile is usable. FirstRunView counts step 2 only with `app.hasProfile` (quality !== 'empty'). Live, scenario mailbox-only: Profil anlegen, fill Name (and Rolle), Speichern. The bar shows "Gespeichert." plus "Weiter zum ersten Abruf" while the head says "Ohne Kompetenzen". The button leads to the first run, where step 2 is still open with "Ohne Kompetenzen wird nichts bewertet." and the primary "Profil öffnen", which sends the user straight back (screenshot t6-after-next.png).
repro: ?platform=windows&scenario=mailbox-only, Profil anlegen, type only a name, Speichern, then press "Weiter zum ersten Abruf".
fix: Offer the way on only when the saved profile counts: `saved && app.state?.firstRun && app.hasProfile`. Otherwise the competence section's hint already says what is missing.

The code agrees: ProfileView.svelte:69 ignores app.hasProfile, while FirstRunView uses it for the step.
verifierNotes.betterFix: The proposed fix is right: `saved && app.state?.firstRun && app.hasProfile`. The competence section's hint already says what is missing.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced (t04.js, scenario mailbox-only): Profil anlegen, name and role only, Speichern. The bar shows "Gespeichert." with "Weiter zum ersten Abruf" while the head badge says "Ohne Kompetenzen". The button leads to the first run, where step 2 is still open with "Ohne Kompetenzen wird nichts bewertet." and "Profil öffnen". ProfileView.svelte:69 does not check app.hasProfile. title: An unreadable country value is shown unlike every other chip or number field
evidence: Since the countries became a chip field (f0e3124), their Field takes only the backend refusal (ProfileEditor.svelte:591, `invalid={fieldError?.field === 'countries'}`), and the file's unreadable value is a separate ValueNote (615-621). Wunschregionen, Wunschbranchen, Orte and the number fields use `error={errorOf(...)}`, `action={removeOf(...)}` and `invalid={errorOf(...) !== null}`. In the profile-unreadable scenario (t3-criteria.png) the number fields show a red edge with "Wert entfernen" under the text on the left. Einsatzländer has no red edge, and its "Wert entfernen" sits at the far right of the line, in the same block.
repro: ?platform=windows&scenario=profile-unreadable, Profil, Ausschlusskriterien: compare Mindest-Tagessatz with Einsatzländer.
fix: Treat countries like regions: error={errorOf('countries')}, action={removeOf('countries')}, invalid={errorOf('countries') !== null}, and drop the ValueNote loop for it.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in the profile-unreadable scenario (screenshot t05-criteria.png). Einsatzländer has 0 invalid markers while Mindest-Tagessatz and Wunschregionen have 2 each, and every other field holding an unread value has a red edge. Einsatzländer does not. The placement part of the evidence is weaker. The countries "Wert entfernen" sits at the far right, but so does the one of the full-width Field Wunschregionen (x=583 of 678). Only the half-width number fields wrap it under the text. The real inconsistency is the missing red edge and aria-invalid, and that the note is a ValueNote instead of the Field's error and action.
verifierNotes.betterFix: The proposed fix is right: error={errorOf('countries')}, action={removeOf('countries')}, invalid={errorOf('countries') !== null} on both the Field and the ChipInput, and drop the countries ValueNote loop. errorOf already puts the backend refusal first, and countries problems are never entry problems.

verifierNotes.note: The inconsistency is real, but the evidence overstates it. In the profile-unreadable scenario the countries field has no red edge and its input has no aria-invalid (t05.js; t05-criteria.png), while Mindest-Tagessatz, Wunschregionen and Orte have both. The note is also not linked through aria-describedby: the input points at {id}-countries-message, which does not exist, because ValueNote gets no id. The position claim is wrong: Wunschregionen, which uses Field's action, also puts "Wert entfernen" at the far right (x 583 in a 678 px row). The number fields wrap it under the text only because their pair columns are narrow. The layout of Field and ValueNote is identical.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Apply the proposed fix: error={errorOf('countries')}, action={removeOf('countries')}, invalid={errorOf('countries') !== null}, and drop the ValueNote loop for countries. A countries problem is never an `entry`, so at most one exists.

title: At the minimum window width the DACH button squeezes the countries field to a sliver
evidence: .countries (ProfileEditor.svelte:882-891) is a non-wrapping flex row: the field flexes and the button keeps its intrinsic width. Measured at 480 px (the minimum window): countries field 144 px (Chromium) / 135 px (WebKit), narrower than the 185 px button beside it, and 90 px tall because the two chips stack. Every other chip field in the form is 333-341 px wide and 36 px tall (see t5-webkit-480-section-criteria.png). This also breaks "every field of a block is 36 px" at that width; the harness checks only min-height.
repro: Viewport 480x900, ?platform=windows, Profil, Ausschlusskriterien.
fix: Let the row wrap, or put the button under the field in a narrow container (@container width < ~520px), so the field keeps the full width like its neighbours.

verifierNotes.note: Measured at 480x900. In Chromium the countries field is 144x90 px next to a 185x36 DACH button; in WebKit it is 135x90 next to 186x36. Werkzeuge, Orte and Wunschregionen are 341 px (Chromium) and 333 px (WebKit) wide and 36 px tall. The screenshot shows the two chips stacked in the narrow box. The cause is the .countries flex row, which does not wrap (ProfileEditor.svelte, .countries).
verifierNotes.betterFix: Use the breakpoint .pair already uses. Below @container (width >= 520px) set .countries to flex-direction: column with align-items: flex-start, so the field keeps the full width and DACH hinzufügen sits under it. Keep the current row from 520 px up. Plain flex-wrap would not wrap, because the field has flex: 1 and min-width: 0, unless it also gets a flex-basis.

verifierNotes.note: Measured (t06.js, default scenario, DE and AT chosen). At 480 px the countries field is 144x90 in Chromium and 135x90 in WebKit, next to a 185 px DACH button, while the other chip fields are 341/333x36. At 560 px it is still 224x62, and it only reaches 36 px tall at 640 px. .countries is a non-wrapping flex row. Screenshot: t06-chromium-480.png.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Give .countries flex-wrap: wrap and give the field a basis (for example flex: 1 1 calc(var(--stat-min) * 2)), or stack the button under the field in the existing @container below 520px, so the field keeps the full width of its neighbours.

title: Country search says "Kein Land mit diesem Namen." for chosen countries and common names
evidence: `matches` drops chosen options (ChipInput.svelte:104), and `nothing` (111) is true whenever no unchosen option matches. With Deutschland already a chip, typing "Deutsch" or "Deutschland" shows "Kein Land mit diesem Namen." next to the Deutschland chip (live, t7-chosen-again.png). The terms (ProfileEditor.svelte:158-164) are only the catalog names and the ISO code, so UK, England, Britain, United States, Vereinigte Staaten, Amerika and Holland all say there is no such country (live, in de and en). The engine itself reads uk, england, united states and vereinigte staaten (engine.rs COUNTRIES).
repro: ?platform=windows, Profil, Einsatzländer: type Deutschland, then UK.
fix: Do not say "no country" when the text matches a chosen one (say nothing, or that it is already chosen). Add the engine's alias names to each option's terms.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium with Deutschland and Österreich already chosen. "Deutsch" and "Deutschland" show profile-countries-none ("Kein Land mit diesem Namen.") with no options. So do UK, England, Holland, United States, Vereinigte Staaten and Amerika. The cause is in the code: matches drops chosen options (ChipInput.svelte:104), nothing is true for any text with no unchosen match (line 111), and the terms are only the two catalog names plus the code. The engine itself reads uk, england, united states and vereinigte staaten.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Compute nothing against every option, chosen or not. When the text matches only chosen countries, say nothing, which is less text than an "already chosen" line. Take the extra search names from the same single country list proposed for ui-forms-03, for example as an alias table next to the catalogs or sent over IPC, so the suggestions and the engine never drift apart again.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in de and en (t07.js). With Deutschland chosen, "Deutsch", "Deutschland" and "Germany" all show "Kein Land mit diesem Namen." / "No country by this name." UK, England, Britain, United States, Vereinigte Staaten, Amerika and Holland show the same, while GB, US and Schweiz work. ChipInput `matches` drops chosen options, and `nothing` is true whenever no unchosen option matches.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Work out `nothing` against all options, chosen ones included, so a chosen country says nothing. Add the aliases (UK, England, Britain, United States, Vereinigte Staaten, Amerika, Holland, Czech Republic) to the options' terms, ideally from the same single name list the fix for ui-forms-03 introduces in core.

title: "Noch leer" marks Ausschlusskriterien of a new profile and of a file full of unreadable criteria
evidence: The criteria section uses `empty={noCriteria}` (ProfileEditor.svelte:256-260, 545) without the `thin &&` gate every other block has. It also counts only readable values. Live: a new profile (scenario no-profile, Profil anlegen) flags only section-criteria with the warning badge "Noch leer", although the section sentences say only Kompetenzen are needed. In profile-unreadable, the same badge sits above nine "In der Datei stand ..." notes (t3-criteria.png).
repro: ?platform=windows&scenario=no-profile, Profil, Profil anlegen, look at the section headings.
fix: Gate it like the others (thin && noCriteria), and count unreadable problems of the block as content.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium. With no-profile and Profil anlegen, the only badge is on section-criteria ("Ausschlusskriterien | Noch leer"), although only the competences are needed. In profile-unreadable the same badge sits above the unread-value notes (t05-criteria.png). The cause is in the code: empty={noCriteria} has no gate, and noCriteria counts only readable values. One caveat: the missing thin gate is partly deliberate. ProfileView's ELSEWHERE comment says the engine's noCriteria warning is "said at its section", so a good profile without criteria is meant to show the badge. Gating with thin && noCriteria would drop that.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Gate on an existing form rather than on thin: empty={quality !== null && noCriteria && problems.every((p) => !CRITERIA_FIELDS.has(p.field))}. CRITERIA_FIELDS covers minDayRate, targetYears, countries, contracts, remoteOutside, minSalary, permanentRemoteMin and permanentPlaces. An untouched new form (quality null) then marks nothing, which is consistent with the other sections. A good profile without criteria keeps the engine's noCriteria meaning, and a file whose criteria exist but do not read is not called empty.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced (t08.js). For a new profile (no-profile, Profil anlegen), section-criteria is the only section with "Noch leer", although the competences hint says only that block is needed and ProfileView says a new form says nothing before it has something. In profile-unreadable, the badge sits above 8 unreadable-value alerts in the same section. The ungated badge is partly intended: ProfileView's ELSEWHERE set routes the engine's noCriteria warning to this section, so a good stored profile without criteria is meant to be marked. For that reason the proposed `thin && noCriteria` would lose that warning.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Use `empty={quality !== null && noCriteria && !problems.some((p) => CRITERIA_FIELDS.has(p.field))}`. That keeps the engine's noCriteria mark for stored profiles, keeps an untouched new form quiet, and does not call a block with unreadable file values empty. Also align ProfileSection's doc ("when a thin profile leaves it empty") with this.

title: Four profile warning texts are never shown, and the table is not typed per code
evidence: profile.warning.noCompetences, fewCompetences, noCriteria and focusTrimmed (de.ts ~505-513 and the en mirror) are read only through warningText. Its two callers exclude these codes (ProfileView.svelte:356-365 ELSEWHERE; checks map only FieldProblems), and the places that say them use other keys (qualityText, profile.empty, field.focusTrimmed). grep finds no other use. The table is `satisfies Record<string, Text>`, so the de.ts header's promise ("Every code ... has exactly one text here ... a new code without a text is a type error") does not hold for profile warnings.
repro: grep -rn "warningText\|profile.warning" ui/src (outside the catalogs).
fix: Remove the four unused texts (both catalogs), or generate a ProfileWarningCode union (ts-rs) and type the table with it.

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. warningText is called only from ProfileHeader, with headWarnings (which excludes noCompetences, fewCompetences, noCriteria and focusTrimmed through ELSEWHERE), and from ProfileView:343, with fieldProblems notices (only criterionNotUnderstood and availabilityNotUnderstood). Nothing else reads t.profile.warning apart from regionWithoutPlaces. Notice.code is a plain string (ts-rs), and the table is `satisfies Record<string, Text>`, so the de.ts header's promise that every code has a typed text does not hold here.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Do not simply delete the four texts: that would widen the gap between the codes in the IPC and the catalog. Better: export ProfileWarningCode through ts-rs, type both catalog tables as Record<ProfileWarningCode, Text> so every code keeps exactly one text, and keep warningText as the single way in. If the four codes should never be spoken, stop sending them in understood.warnings (the UI computes quality and emptiness itself) and drop them together with their texts.

verifierNotes.note: It is true that noCompetences, fewCompetences, noCriteria and focusTrimmed never reach warningText: ProfileView ELSEWHERE filters them from the head, and checks maps only field problems. That is deliberate, since they are said elsewhere by design. title: 'Gelöschte Jobs' means two opposite things: restorable jobs in the Papierkorb, and jobs that never come back

The archive reader (de.ts:615) says '…bis du sie zurückholst oder löschst', while the action is named 'In den Papierkorb' and 'löschen' is used only for 'Endgültig löschen'.
fix: Use one word per state: 'Jobs im Papierkorb' for trashed jobs, and 'Endgültig gelöschte Jobs kommen nicht wieder' for purged ones. Say 'in den Papierkorb legst' in the archive line. Same in en.ts.
repro: Open Papierkorb with nothing selected (reader text), then choose Endgültig löschen on a job (dialog text).

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. de.ts:616 and :618-619 use 'Gelöschte Jobs' for restorable trash contents, de.ts:631 uses it for purged jobs that never come back, and de.ts:1358 (autoEmptyTrashHint) uses it again for the purged ones. en.ts mirrors this ('Deleted jobs stay here' and 'Deleted jobs never come back'). The archive line says 'löschst' while the action is named 'In den Papierkorb'.
verifierNotes.betterFix: One word per state, in de and en. place.reader.trash: 'Jobs im Papierkorb bleiben hier, bis du sie wiederherstellst oder den Papierkorb leerst.' place.trashFor: 'Jobs im Papierkorb werden nach n Tagen endgültig gelöscht.' actions.purgeText: 'Endgültig gelöschte Jobs kommen nicht wieder, auch nicht mit alten Alert-Mails.' place.reader.archive: '… bis du sie zurückholst oder in den Papierkorb legst.' settings autoEmptyTrashHint: 'Jobs im Papierkorb sind danach endgültig weg.' Mirror these in en.ts ('Jobs in the trash …', 'Jobs deleted forever …').

title: Papierkorb: the row shows the deletion date, the reader the mail date, both unlabelled
evidence: JobRow.svelte:122-124 uses trashedAt in the trash, while the reader facts use the mail date. Live (s22.js): for freelance-900411 just moved to the trash, row date 'jetzt', reader facts '… freelance.de · vor 5 Stunden', place line 'Im Papierkorb, wird nach 30 Tagen gelöscht'.
fix: Show the same date in both places or name them ('gelöscht jetzt'). In the reader's place line, give the date the job goes for good (e.g. 'wird am 25.10. gelöscht').
repro: Move a job to the trash, open Papierkorb, open it, and move the pointer off the row: the row says 'jetzt', the reader 'vor 5 Stunden'.

verifierNotes.note: Part of this is intended. PLAN (Schema 5 section) says the trash sorts by 'the day it went there', and JobRow.svelte:122-124 shows that sort date on purpose, while the reader facts show the mail date like in every other place. What the code does prove is a real gap. The place line (Reader.svelte:440-445) always says 'wird nach 30 Tagen gelöscht' and ignores trashedAt, although auto-empty counts from trashed_at (store/marks.rs:209). A job trashed 29 days ago still reads '30 Tagen', and nothing in the reader explains the row's 'jetzt'.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Leave the row date as it is (documented). Compute the place line from job.trashedAt + autoEmptyTrashDays and give the concrete day, e.g. 'Im Papierkorb, wird am 24.10. endgültig gelöscht' (en: 'In the trash, deleted forever on 24 Oct'). That fixes the misleading fixed '30 Tagen' and ties the reader to the trash date.

title: 'Wiederherstellen' always puts a job into Jobs, also one that was deleted from the Archiv
evidence: actions.ts:37-42 maps restore to 'inbox'. Live (s25.js): archive linkedin-4100200301, delete it from the Archiv, restore it in the Papierkorb. The job's place is now 'inbox' and the toast says 'wiederhergestellt'. Mail's 'put back' returns a message to where it came from. The job also restarts its auto-archive clock in the inbox.
fix: Remember the place a job left for the trash (like Unmove) and restore there, or name the action 'Zurück zu Jobs' when the target is the inbox.
repro: Archive a job, open Archiv, move it to the trash, open Papierkorb and click Wiederherstellen: it appears under Jobs, not in the Archiv.

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. actions.ts:37-42 maps restore to 'inbox'. The backend move to Inbox sets archived_at = NULL and inbox_at = now (store/marks.rs:108-110), which resets the auto-archive clock. Moving to the trash sets only trashed_at and keeps archived_at (marks.rs:116, PLAN: 'trashed_at wins over archived_at'). So the store already knows the job came from the Archiv, but 'Wiederherstellen' ignores it.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Make restore a backend move that only clears trashed_at (`trashed_at = NULL`, keeping archived_at and inbox_at). The job then returns to exactly where it lay, in the Archiv or the inbox, without a new auto-archive clock. The UI's restore target only affects the toast and the counts, which a reload after the move covers. This touches `move_jobs` or a new Place variant (shared files, integrator). Renaming the action would not fix the mismatch.

title: Copying the reader's facts line starts with a hidden ' · '
evidence: Every fact carries its separator in front (Reader.svelte:507-511), and the first one is only clipped visually (:1003-1012). Live (s28.js): triple-click on the facts gives ' · Hanseatic Holding GmbH · Hamburg · …' in Chromium and WebKit (WebKit also on a drag selection).
fix: Render no separator before the first fact (index > 0), or make the leading one user-select: none.
repro: Open a job, triple-click the facts line under the title, Ctrl+C, paste: the text starts with ' · '.

verifierNotes.note: Reproduced in Chromium and WebKit. Triple-clicking the reader's .facts selects ' · Hanseatic Holding GmbH · Hamburg · 6 Monate · 60 % remote'. The first fact's separator is only clipped (margin-left -20px, overflow hidden), so it is still in the copied text.
verifierNotes.betterFix: Render the separator only for index > 0 in the `dotted` snippet, and add `text-indent: var(--space-20)` to .facts-line. The first line then starts at 0 without a dot, while wrapped lines keep the -20px shift that clips their leading dot. Combine this with the inline-block .fact from live-jobs-02 and check both engines.

title: Abrufen from Archiv or Papierkorb puts the run result ('2 neu', '1 passt gut') on top of the archive list, with no way to the new jobs
evidence: JobsView.svelte:203-207 shows the run card in every place, and the RunCard pills are not actionable. Live (s20.js): Archiv, click Abrufen. After the run, the Archiv column shows 'Abruf fertig 09:30 2 neu 1 passt gut' above '1 Job im Archiv' (screenshot s20-archive-done-chromium.png). Reaching the new jobs takes the sidebar and then Neu.
fix: Let the 'n neu' pill open Neu, or switch to Jobs/Neu when a fetch is started from the Archiv or Papierkorb.
repro: Open Archiv, click Abrufen, wait: the result card sits above the archived jobs and its '2 neu' is not clickable.

verifierNotes.note: The code proves it. JobsView.svelte:203-207 shows the RunCard whenever shell.runCard is set, in every place, and the 'n neu' and 'n passt gut' pills (RunCard.svelte:231-238) are plain badges. Since the user removed the sidebar count, this card is the only sign in the Archiv or Papierkorb that new jobs arrived, and it offers no way to them. The severity is low (Jobs in the sidebar is one click away).
verifierNotes.betterFix: Do not switch places on the user's behalf when a fetch starts from the Archiv or Papierkorb. Instead, only while the place is not the inbox, give the finished card one quiet ghost button with a verb phrase ('Neue Jobs zeigen' / 'Show new jobs') that calls jobs.setFacet('new') and navigates to Jobs. Keep the pills as they are.
